name: Norway
sources: GDP about $118bn and population 4.24m (World Bank / SSB, 1990).
Inflation 4.1% (SSB consumer price index, 1990). Norges Bank held short rates near 11% defending the krone's unilateral ECU peg announced in October 1990.

Tax revenue 41% of GDP (OECD Revenue Statistics, 1990); general government gross debt 32% of GDP, low because petroleum revenue was already running a structural surplus. The Government Petroleum Fund act followed in 1990 with the first transfer in 1996.
Oil 1.70 mbd (Norwegian Petroleum Directorate, 1990) - Statfjord, Gullfaks and Oseberg. Norway was the largest producer in Western Europe after the United Kingdom and passed it later in the decade.
Defence 2.9% of GDP (NATO defence expenditure series, 1990). Strength 9: a small conscript force whose weight in the alliance was its position on the Kola flank and the Norwegian Sea, not its size.
Norway rejected EC membership in 1972 and would reject it again in 1994; it was an EFTA state negotiating the European Economic Area in 1990.
